ai.description: This gecko reaches 12–15 cm. It features a pale yellow to brownish body with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a thick, fleshy tail. It is distinguished by movable eyelids and clawed digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eublepharis fuscus* is best distinguished by the absence of a distinct white nuchal collar, which is present in most other Indian *Eublepharis* species.
ai.habitat: *Eublepharis fuscus* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky scrublands in Western India, typically found at elevations ranging from near sea level to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Eublepharis fuscus* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from rocky crevices at night to forage for insects and small invertebrates across its arid habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eublepharis fuscus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eublepharis fuscus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Karnataka at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
